clue.text: As a player, stroke something soft, then accept the applause

parts.note: down is the soft fluffy feathering used in pillows
a performer will bow to acknowledge clapping

explanation.surface: A performer strokes something soft and then takes a bow at the end of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase: a stroke made by a string player, the bow drawn downwards across the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist's bowing technique includes a stroke drawn from frog to tip, the term for one such bowing stroke.

clue.text: Ignore broadcast amid racket

indicators.note: amid tells us the scattering word sits in the middle of the noise word

parts.note: a racket is a loud noise, a din
to broadcast seed is to scatter it, to sow

explanation.surface: Someone tunes out a radio broadcast in the middle of a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' tempts as a radio term but here it is the farming sense of scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate or refuse to acknowledge someone is to ignore them as your own.

clue.text: False hair and artificial leg, Othello turns up for play!

parts.note: a wig is a hairpiece

indicators.note: artificial means made up, so these letters are made into another arrangement
in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: An actor playing Othello with a wig and prosthetic leg trips over on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artificial' rearranges LEG into GLE; 'turns up' reverses MOOR into the last four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Room to manoeuvre or flexibility is called play, as in some slack in a rope.

clue.text: Nationals Blessed and May catching Minnelli up

indicators.note: catching means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: Brian Blessed the actor and Brian May the Queen guitarist are two Brians

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: Liza Minnelli is the singer and actress

explanation.surface: A list of celebrities: two famous Brians grabbing Liza Minnelli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blessed and May' are both surnames of famous Brians, the actor and the Queen guitarist, so together they give a plural; 'up' turns the singer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationals are citizens of a country, here people from Brazil.

clue.text: Country not always upset over leadership in government? No!

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first part above the next
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards
not tells us to leave the short word for always out of the country

parts.note: Norway is a Scandinavian country
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

indicators.note: leadership points to the leading letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A question of whether a country is constantly upset over who leads its government.
explanation.walkthrough: NORWAY loses AY to give NORW; 'upset' turns that into WRON, sitting over G.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclaiming that something is incorrect is the same as shouting a flat denial.

clue.text: Hairy, hairy thing stopped to pluck third of hairs

parts.note: a bear is a famously shaggy animal

indicators.note: plucking removes a letter, as you would pull out a hair

parts.note: a machine that died has stopped

indicators.note: third of points to the third letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A hairy creature stops to pluck some of its hairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The third letter of 'hairs' is I, pulled from DIED to leave DED.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a growth on the chin makes a face hairy.

clue.text: See company of writers cornering market in Irish

indicators.note: cornering means hemming the other piece in

parts.note: Bic is a company that makes ballpoint pens

indicators.note: in puts the shop word inside the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: a shop is a market for goods

explanation.surface: A pen manufacturer trying to dominate a market in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a noun here, a bishop's area of authority, not the verb; 'in' and 'cornering' each nest one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the district or office under a bishop's authority, the diocese.

clue.text: A short jumper in style going over head?

indicators.note: short means cutting off the final letter

parts.note: a frog is a jumping creature, not a sweater

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a cropped sweater pulled over their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a British sweater (pullover), but it is the frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushy rounded hairstyle is one kind of style worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Despised philanthropist has to improve, when grammatically failing?

definitions.meaning: a sneer word for a well-meaning meddler
do better, said ungrammatically, becomes do plus a wrong comparative of good

explanation.surface: A disliked benefactor is told to improve his grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is a scornful label for an interfering, self-righteous charitable person; the second sense is a botched comparative.

clue.text: Brilliant in sticks?

definitions.meaning: the explosive is sold in stick-shaped cartridges

explanation.definitionFit: The explosive comes packed in sticks, and the word is slang for something sensational or excellent.

clue.text: Greek character writing name (Martin?) backwards, minimum of Greek in it

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the reversed surname
backwards means the surname is read right to left

parts.note: Martin Amis was a British novelist, so Amis is a writing name

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its single first letter

explanation.surface: A Greek letter written as a novelist's name in reverse, with a bit of Greek in it.
explanation.walkthrough: AMIS backwards is SIMA; the G goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, the S sound, is a Greek character.

clue.text: Hormone required, or one gets high

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so these letters are in a giddy jumble

explanation.surface: Taking a hormone, or else one gets high.
explanation.definitionFit: The female sex hormone is a well-known example of a hormone.

clue.text: See 24
See 2
Slow eel reacted when tickled

indicators.note: a tickled eel would squirm, so these letters wriggle into a new order

explanation.surface: A sluggish eel reacted when somebody tickled it.
explanation.definitionFit: To slow is to reduce speed, the verb's synonym.

clue.text: Partner having left, really in debt, sums wasted, money spent!

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters are reshaped
having left means the partner word departs from the next word

parts.note: an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: After a partner walks out, someone is deep in debt with money squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLY leaves 'really' to give RE, mixed with INDEBT and SUMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment out of funds is money paid away, a sum laid out.

clue.text: Meals on wheels serving maggot up with raven porridge

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from the bottom

parts.note: a grub is an insect larva like a maggot

indicators.note: porridge is a mash, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A disgusting meal of maggot and raven served up as porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meals on wheels' is a British charity service delivering food, but here it is a mobile snack van. GRUB reversed is BURG; RAVEN mixed gives ERVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile fast-food van selling hamburgers provides food from a vehicle.

clue.text: Essential to Knesset, a report that's written up works

indicators.note: written up in a down clue means reading bottom to top
the essential part is the letters inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A report that is essential to the Israeli parliament is drafted.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'Knesset, a report' backwards: (TR)OPERATES(SENK).
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that runs or functions is said to work.

clue.text: Old singers assigned parts, then deserter given one

parts.note: actors are cast when assigned their roles
a rat is someone who deserts their side
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Singers given roles, with a defector added to the company.
explanation.definitionFit: Male sopranos of the past, castrated in boyhood, were celebrated opera singers.

clue.text: One so puffed up right to punch man with beauty

indicators.note: punching goes into, so the letter goes inside the chessman

parts.note: a pawn is a chessman
a cracker is slang for a stunner, a beauty

explanation.surface: Someone full of themselves punches a man who has a beauty with him.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese-restaurant snack is deep-fried so that it puffs up light and airy.

clue.text: Englishman in Normandy, say, can't be trusted with gold after uprising

indicators.note: after uprising, in a down clue, the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: one who fibs tells lies and can't be trusted
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An English visitor to Normandy is untrustworthy, coming with gold after a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: FIBSOR read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: French slang for the English is roast beef, a jokey label a person in France might use.

clue.text: Trouble over cardinal being worshipped

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
cardinal red is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Trouble arises over a cardinal who is venerated.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone revered and loved deeply is worshipped.

clue.text: Blight a schedule

parts.note: rot is decay, a blight

explanation.surface: Something ruins a timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster of duties is a schedule saying who does what when.

clue.text: Spring back for a little extra time

parts.note: to spring is to leap
to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: Clocks spring back in time, giving a bit more.
explanation.definitionFit: One extra second is occasionally added to clocks to keep them aligned with Earth's rotation.

clue.text: Slug, say, with duck sauce

parts.note: a slug is an example of a garden pest
a duck is a zero score in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: A slug appearing in duck sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The basil-and-pine-nut paste is a sauce for pasta.

clue.text: One required to trudge through honey, perhaps, eating starter in fragrant dish?

indicators.note: eating means the boot phrase takes the next letter inside itself

parts.words: One required to trudge through honey, perhaps
parts.note: a whimsical rubber boot for a bee, needed to trudge through sticky honey

indicators.note: starter means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone wading through honey to eat a starter in a perfumed dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A wellington is a British name for a rubber boot (galosh); a bee would need one to wade through honey. The F goes inside, after BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak fillet baked in pastry is a classic dish named after a duke.

clue.text: Duck on edge of roof remains for the pot?

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
eaves are the overhanging edge of a roof

explanation.surface: A duck sits on the edge of a roof, its remains destined for the cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' suggests a cooking pot but it is a teapot.
explanation.definitionFit: What is left in the bottom of a teapot after brewing is the remnant of the brew.

clue.text: Though not dawning, shepherd's warning?

indicators.note: not dawning means the word loses its first letter, its dawn

parts.note: a lamber is a shepherd who tends ewes at lambing time

explanation.surface: A twist on the weather rhyme where red sky at morning is the shepherd's warning.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the saying 'red sky in the morning, shepherd's warning'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a traffic light the yellow-orange light is the caution colour, telling drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Set well back, marsh east of Senegalese capital

indicators.note: in an across clue, east of means placed to the right
capital means the first letter of the next word
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: fit means healthy, well
a fen is a marsh

explanation.surface: A well is set back from a marsh east of Senegal's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To set or harden, as a jelly does, is to become rigid.

clue.text: Retired female minister into dictionary is stuffed!

indicators.note: into places the reversed pieces inside the dictionary abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: A retired female minister gets into the dictionary and is stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: F plus REV reversed is VERF.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuffed means having eaten too much food.
